facts: This appeal is directed against the judgment of the High Court of Allahabad confirming the convictions and sentences awarded to the four appellants by the trial court.

These four appellants along with two other were tried for offences punishable under Section 302 read with Section 149, Section 324 read with Section 149, Section 325 read with Section 149 and Section 323 read with Section 149 IPC.
The trial court convicted the four appellants herein under Section 302 read with Section 149 and sentenced each of them to undergo imprisonment for life.
They were also convicted under Sections 147, 148 and Section 324 read with Section 149 IPC.
The trial court acquitted the other two accused.
The convicted accused as well as State preferred appeals.

The High Court while dismissing the appeal by the State converted the conviction of the other four namely appellants herein to one under Section 304 Part II read with Section 149 and sentenced each of them to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of five years.
The other minor convictions and sentences were confirmed and thus partly allowed the appeal.
issues: Whether the High Court was correct in convicting the appellants under Section 304 Part II simpliciter?
Whether the prosecution case has been satisfactorily proved?
petitioner_arguments: The appellants contended that the High Court had rejected the substratum of the prosecution case and that the appellants are entitled to a complete acquittal even on the findings of the High Court.
It was argued that there was no material to convict any of the appellants under Section 304 Part II simpliciter as there is absolutely no scope to infer complicity in the crime.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution case is that Middu, one of the acquitted accused, was married to one Smt. Hajra.
It was argued that the appellants were members of an unlawful assembly and that they caused injuries to the deceased and others during a free fight.
court_reasoning: The High Court having noted the injuries on the accused observed: 'From the evidence on record and particularly from the facts that as many as four persons from the side of the accused were also injured in the incident, it is quite likely that a free fight occurred between the parties on account of the above dispute and during the course of the said fight, the complainant's party was worked.'
The High Court convicted all the four appellants under Section 304 part II simpliciter without any further discussion as to the part played by each of the accused.
holding: The convictions and sentences passed against the appellants are set aside.
